A paraphonic SawX stab: the main envelope opens the closed low-pass filter on each note and closes it again, with no sustain. The Cycling Envelope pushes Saw Mod, and key position and pressure open the filter further.

In GitP/A/Session/26/11/22-Sun, Tactile Techno is on the third Launchpad/Sequencer track and is reshaped heavily while its take records, from 02:20 to 04:08. The session MIDI records Attack and Decay/Release from 02:51. Next come the Cycling Envelope's Amount, Fall, Rise and Hold by 03:21. Then Shape, Timbre and Wave move from 03:33 to the end of the take; on SawX these knobs set Noise, Shape and Saw Mod.
The October capture predates these edits, so it documents the factory starting point rather than the sound in the episode.

Simulates the low-battery chirp of a smoke or fire alarm. Made as a timing cue for GitP/Ceremon/y/Fallveter on 2026-11-14 Sat, following the alarm-cue idea in Making/Music/Log/26/11/11-Wed.
Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/02 SuperWave with the waves set to sine.
Each chirp is the highest G on the keyboard with octave +3, G7, at the minimum sequencer gate length of 10 ms. Attack and decay are at zero.
The chirps recorded in GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat sound at about 3140 Hz, close to G7's 3136 Hz.
Set the tempo to 60 BPM for the intervals below.
Sequence A chirps once every 60 seconds.
Sequence B chirps once every 30 seconds.
Low-battery alarms commonly chirp at one of these two intervals.
